biggest_catch: Dscout's own terms say each mission sets its own payment terms - the platform publishes no concrete worker pay figures and no payout schedule.
catches: No official concrete pay: 'Each Mission will have its own set of terms as to payment, if any, for participation.'
No official payout schedule found in dscout's scout-facing terms.
You are paid only upon completion of the mission to the researcher's specifications.
dscout 'reserves the right to not compensate Scouts who fail to perform the Mission requirements in a complete and timely manner.'
All per-mission dollar amounts in circulation ($25–$200) come from third-party reviews, not dscout.

c1.evidence: Dscout's own Scout Terms: 'Each Mission will have its own set of terms as to payment, if any, for participation.' No concrete worker pay figures published.

c2.evidence: No official payout schedule in dscout's scout-facing terms or pages.

c3.evidence: Free to become a scout; no upfront fee documented.

c4.evidence: Fails both the official-pay and official-timing requirements.

eligibility: Become a scout via the free dscout app or site; apply to missions; be selected by a researcher.
maximize: Dscout is rejected here because its official terms publish no concrete worker pay figures and no payout schedule. If official figures ever appear, apply to diary and live missions (the highest-pay categories per third-party reports) and complete missions exactly to the researcher's specifications - dscout reserves the right to withhold pay for incomplete work.
notes: Dscout's own terms deliberately delegate payment terms to each mission's researcher, so there is no platform-level concrete pay or timing to verify. All dollar figures in circulation are third-party claims.
